audit.whatIsWrong: diff says FAV while diffRating says 8/10 and both difficulty lines say 'Hard matchup', at a 60% win rate. Four chart rows also disagree with the packet and with the content layer's own whys: whys[2] and whys[3] both begin 'Even —' but render as Camille, whys[4] says 'Camille owns it' but renders as Neeko, and whys[6] says 'You reclaim it' but renders as Camille.
audit.why: Level 6 is the single most important row here and the page had it backwards — it told a Neeko player she wins the level at which the same page says Camille anchors her for a 1v1.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Neeko / Skill / Skill / Skill / Camille / Camille / Neeko as matched pairs; diff EVEN, diffRating 6/10, carryRating 8/10, tone to the even colour, both difficulty lines rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] sold Level 6 as a Neeko spike and phases[5]/[6] carried boilerplate about a Stormsurge spike the content layer never builds.
audit.why: The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90s and anchors the target to an area — the level 6 spike is hers, and the row Neeko actually reclaims is 2+ items on AoE teamfighting.
audit.corrected: phases[2] through phases[4] and phases[6] rewritten on Hookshot's 16s, the anchor, and the AoE flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4], spikes[2] and mid all describe Pop Blossom as a 'long, interruptible channel'. Riot's text says only that it has a short preparation, and that the preparation is HIDDEN while Neeko is disguised — the opposite read. mid and wants.you[2] again claim 'W invis', which Neeko does not have, and late refers to 'your shield value' when she has no shield. Nothing on the page carried the interaction that actually matters: Inherent Glamour breaks on immobilizing crowd control, so Hookshot's knock-up strips a disguised Neeko's cover.
audit.why: A player told her ult is interruptible will hold it; a player told she has invisibility will walk in with a clone; and neither knows that Hookshot is Camille's answer to the disguise.
audit.corrected: Preparation language corrected everywhere it appeared, invisibility replaced with the clone, and the Hookshot-breaks-disguise rule written into report[5].t and dontsFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal, against Tactical Sweep healing her on the outer half of every cone.
audit.why: Her sustain is what turns a whiffed root into a lost extended trade — the page even says so in early without offering the item answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] writes the ult as 'Hextech Ultimatum'.
audit.why: The real name carries the article — The Hextech Ultimatum.
audit.corrected: Fixed in wants.foe[1]; spikes[2] already had it right.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay even — you out-waveclear her with Q and poke, but you can't all-in without ult and she'll just E away from a telegraphed root. Level 6 flips to her: Pop Blossom (R) has a long, interruptible wind-up, and the instant you channel she E-hookshots in or R-cages you into a 1v1 where her W heal and true damage beat your squishy body. Don't try to out-trade her ult window — use W invis/clone to dodge her engage, ult only to disengage or in a gank, and look to roam with disguise instead of forcing the solo kill she's built to win.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay even — you out-waveclear her with Q and poke, but you can't all-in without ult and she'll just Hookshot away from a telegraphed root. Level 6 flips to her: Pop Blossom needs a preparation before the knock-up, and the moment it starts she Hookshots in or anchors you with The Hextech Ultimatum into a 1v1 where her W heal and true damage beat your squishy body. Don't out-trade her ult window — send the Shapesplitter clone to bait her engage, ult only to disengage or in a gank, and roam disguised instead of forcing the solo kill she is built to win.

edits.before: You took this lane on tempo and roam pressure, not the late 1v1 — Camille is a hard scaler and at 2+ items her Sheen/Eclipse procs, W true-damage, and R isolation outlast your single Pop Blossom rotation. In a straight side-lane duel she E-dashes your telegraphed root, walls you in, and kills you before your shield value matters. Convert your level-1-through-first-item lead into a turret and team tempo, then play Neeko as a teamfight bomb deleting her clustered backline — never let her catch you alone where her R turns the map into a 1v1 she wins.
edits.after: You took this lane on tempo and roam pressure, not the late 1v1 — Camille is a hard scaler and at 2+ items her Sheen/Eclipse procs, Q true damage and R isolation outlast your single Pop Blossom rotation. In a straight side-lane duel she Hookshots your telegraphed root, anchors you, and kills you before one rotation finishes. Convert your level-1-through-first-item lead into a turret and team tempo, then play Neeko as a teamfight bomb deleting her clustered backline — never let her catch you alone where her R turns the map into a 1v1 she wins.

notes: Two opposite-direction errors about Pop Blossom were on this page at once: it was called a 'long, interruptible channel' three times, when Riot's text says only that it has a short preparation and that the preparation is HIDDEN while disguised. The genuine Camille answer — Hookshot's knock-up is immobilizing CC and therefore breaks Inherent Glamour — was nowhere on the page, and is now in report[5].t and dontsFull[0].d. Four chart rows were wrong in both layers at once. I did NOT write the missingInteractions 'untargetable-dodges-burst' item: The Hextech Ultimatum's derived untargetable and channel flags are both contradicted by Riot's description, which says only that she dashes to the target and anchors them — per the calibration rule I trusted the description. Same for the claim that her R is a channel any CC cancels.
